`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_device_audio.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_audio" }}{{ if eq .DeviceClass "audio" }}
    // ========================================================================
    // HDA GCTL.CRST handshake + CORB/RIRB auto-response
    // hdaudio.sys writes CRST=0 (assert reset), then CRST=1 (deassert).
    // after deassert, we reload STATESTS so codec discovery works.
    // STATESTS lives in the upper 16 bits of the DWORD at 0x0C.
    //
    // CORB/RIRB auto-response: without this, hdaudio.sys polls RIRBWP
    // endlessly waiting for codec responses, generating massive PCIe
    // read TLP traffic that congests the FPGA fabric and throttles
    // DMA throughput to ~80 KB/s. We generate a fake RIRB response
    // for each VERB the driver submits via CORB, so the driver completes init.
    // ========================================================================

    // ---- Register declarations (must precede CRST block and FSM) ----
    reg crst_prev;
    reg  [7:0] rirb_response_fsm;
    reg [63:0] rirb_fake_response;
    reg  [7:0] corbwp_prev;
    reg  [7:0] rirb_pending_count;  // number of VERBs waiting for response
    reg  [7:0] rirb_wp_count;
    reg  [5:0] rirb_response_idx;   // index into response ROM (0-63)
    reg corb_cte_prev, rirb_cte_prev;

    // Internal DMA interface registers (driven by RIRB FSM)
    reg         dma_req_valid_r;
    reg [31:0]  dma_resp_lo_r;
    reg [31:0]  dma_resp_hi_r;
    reg [7:0]   dma_resp_wp_r;
    reg         dma_done_latched;  // latches the 1-cycle dma_done pulse
    reg [27:0]  dma_wait_counter;  // 28-bit: 268,435,455 cycles = ~2.1s @125MHz
    reg         dma_timed_out;
    reg  [15:0] dma_recovery_count; // bridge recovery attempt limit (max 65536)
    reg  [3:0]  dma_round_count;    // rounds restarted from 0x04 (max 16)

    // ---- CRST handshake ----
    // only tracks edges; actual state reset is done by the main FSM
    // to avoid multi-driver conflicts on shared registers.
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            crst_prev <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            crst_prev <= reg_0x00000008[0];
        end
    end

    wire crst_rising  = reg_0x00000008[0] && !crst_prev;  // coming out of reset

    // ========================================================================
    // Fake RIRB response generator (multi-VERB queue, sequence-based ROM)
    //
    // For each VERB the driver submits via CORB (detected by CORBWP changes),
    // we enqueue a fake RIRB response. A counter tracks pending responses;
    // the FSM drains one response at a time. Multiple outstanding VERBs are
    // supported — the driver can submit several CORB entries before we finish
    // responding to the first one.
    //
    // CORBWP delta calculation: the driver may advance CORBWP by N entries
    // in a single write (e.g., submitting multiple VERBs at once). We compute
    // the actual delta to enqueue the correct number of responses.
    //
    // Response ROM: hdaudio.sys sends different VERBs during codec topology
    // discovery and expects different responses. A canned ROM provides a
    // realistic sequence matching CA0132 (Creative Sound Blaster Audigy FX V2).
    // The 64-bit response format:
    //   [63:32] = type (bits [3:0]) | NID (bits [27:4]) | tag (bits [31:28])
    //   [31:0]  = response data (28-bit payload)
    //
    // RIRB response type 0x1 = standard VERB response data.
    // ========================================================================

    // CORBWP change detection: driver submitted new VERB(s).
    wire corb_cte = reg_0x0000004C[1];   // CORBCTL.CORBRUN (bit 1)
    wire rirb_cte  = reg_0x0000005C[1];   // RIRBCTL.RIRBDMAEN (bit 1)
    wire corbwp_changed = (corbwp_prev != reg_0x00000048[7:0]) && corb_cte && rirb_cte;
    // Calculate how many entries the driver added (handles wrap-around at 256)
    wire [7:0] corbwp_delta_raw = reg_0x00000048[7:0] - corbwp_prev;
    // If delta > 32, the driver reset CORBWP without disabling CTE — treat as
    // no new VERBs. Without this, a WP reset enqueues 200+ phantom responses
    // that drain the ROM into the catch-all zone.
    wire [7:0] corbwp_delta = (corbwp_delta_raw > 8'h20) ? 8'h00 : corbwp_delta_raw;

    // CORB/RIRB reinitialization detection: driver disables CTE to reset buffers.
    // When CTE goes low, the driver is reinitializing — reset ROM index and
    // pending state so the next discovery cycle starts fresh.
    wire corb_reinit = corb_cte_prev && !corb_cte;
    wire rirb_reinit = rirb_cte_prev && !rirb_cte;
    wire rb_reinit   = corb_reinit || rirb_reinit;

    // ========================================================================
    // RIRBINTSTS RW1C (write-1-to-clear) detection.
    // RIRBINTSTS (offset 0x60) has IsRW1C=true, so it is excluded from the
    // generic write handler by the (not .IsRW1C) template filter.
    // HD Audio spec requires RIRBINTSTS bit 0 (INTFL) to be RW1C:
    //   write 1 → clear the flag, write 0 → no change.
    //
    // We detect the write here but DON'T write to reg_0x00000060 directly —
    // that would create a multi-driver conflict with the main FSM which also
    // sets INTFL. Instead, we produce a clear request that the main FSM
    // merges into the single reg_0x00000060[0] driver.
    reg rirbintsts_rw1c;
    reg [31:0] hda_wr_data;
    reg [3:0] hda_wr_be;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rirbintsts_rw1c <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            // Detect write to RIRBINTSTS at 0x60
            rirbintsts_rw1c <= wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h00000060;
            hda_wr_data <= wr_data;
            hda_wr_be <= wr_be;
        end
    end

    // Clear request: driver writes 1 to bit 0 → clear INTFL.
    wire intfl_clear_req = rirbintsts_rw1c && hda_wr_be[0] && hda_wr_data[0];

    // CRST rising edge clear request: same as crst_rising
    wire intfl_crst_clear_req = crst_rising;

    // INTFL set request from RIRB response commit FSM.
    // This is a flag that the FSM uses to request INTFL be set to 1.
    // The actual reg_0x00000060[0] write is consolidated in a single always
    // block to avoid multi-driver conflicts.
    reg intfl_set_req;

    // ========================================================================
    // RIRBCTL/RIRBSTS (0x5C) driver write handler.
    // This register is IsRW1C — excluded from generic write logic. We must
    // handle ALL MMIO writes here:
    //   - Control bits [2:0]: CTE (bit 0), OIE (bit 2) — standard writable
    //   - Status bits [10:8]: OIS (bit 8), UIS (bit 9), INTFL (bit 10) — RW1C
    // RW1C for status: driver writes 1 → clear to 0, writes 0 → preserve.
    // Standard write for control: driver writes value → update the bit.
    // ========================================================================
    reg rirbctl_rw1c;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rirbctl_rw1c <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            rirbctl_rw1c <= wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h0000005C;
        end
    end

    // RIRBCTL/RIRBSTS write requests - consumed by main FSM to avoid multi-driver.
    wire rirbctl_wr_rintctl_val = hda_wr_data[0];  // RINTCTL (bit 0)
    wire rirbctl_wr_cte_val = hda_wr_data[1];  // RIRBDMAEN (bit 1)
    wire rirbctl_wr_oie_val = hda_wr_data[2];  // OIC (bit 2)
    wire [2:0] rirbsts_clear_mask = hda_wr_data[10:8];

    // ========================================================================
    // CORBCTL/CORBSTS (0x4C) driver write handler.
    // This register is IsRW1C — excluded from generic write logic. We must
    // handle ALL MMIO writes here:
    //   - Control bits: CTE (bit 7), MEIE (bit 1) — standard writable
    //   - Status bit: RPWP (bit 8) — RW1C
    // RW1C for RPWP: driver writes 1 -> clear to 0, writes 0 -> preserve.
    // Standard write for control: driver writes value -> update the bit.
    // ========================================================================
    reg corbsts_rw1c;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            corbsts_rw1c <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            corbsts_rw1c <= wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h0000004C;
        end
    end

    // CORBCTL/CORBSTS write requests - consumed by write handler to avoid multi-driver.
    wire corbctl_wr_cmeie_val = hda_wr_data[0];
    wire corbctl_wr_run_val = hda_wr_data[1];
    wire corbsts_clear_bit = hda_wr_data[8];

{{ template "bar_impl_device_audio_response_rom" . }}{{ template "bar_impl_device_audio_response_fsm" . }}{{ template "bar_impl_device_audio_interrupts" . }}{{ end }}
{{ end }}

```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_device_audio_interrupts.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_audio_interrupts" }}    // ========================================================================
    // Consolidated INTFL driver — SINGLE source for reg_0x00000060.
    // All INTFL modifications go through here to avoid multi-driver conflicts.
    // Priority: set (response committed) takes precedence over RW1C clear.
    // This ensures the MSI edge is never missed when driver clears INTFL in
    // the same cycle we set it — the set wins, clear applies on next write.
    // CRST/reinit clear still takes absolute priority (full reset).
    // ========================================================================
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            reg_0x00000060 <= 32'h00000000;
        end else if (rb_reinit || intfl_crst_clear_req) begin
            // CRST rising edge or CTE reinit — clear INTFL.
            reg_0x00000060[0] <= 1'b0;
        end else if (intfl_set_req) begin
            // RIRB response committed — set INTFL to notify driver.
            // Takes priority over RW1C clear: if both fire simultaneously,
            // INTFL goes 0→1, triggering MSI edge detection. The driver's
            // clear takes effect on the next write to RIRBINTSTS.
            reg_0x00000060[0] <= 1'b1;
        end else if (intfl_clear_req) begin
            // Driver wrote 1 to RIRBINTSTS[0] (RW1C) — clear INTFL.
            reg_0x00000060[0] <= 1'b0;
        end
        // Default: hold current value (no explicit assignment needed for regs).
    end

    // Port assignments — expose internal regs to module outputs
    assign dma_req_valid   = dma_req_valid_r;
    assign dma_resp_lo     = dma_resp_lo_r;
    assign dma_resp_hi     = dma_resp_hi_r;
    assign dma_resp_wp     = dma_resp_wp_r;
    assign dma_rirb_lbase  = reg_0x00000050;  // RIRBLBASE
    assign dma_rirb_ubase  = reg_0x00000054;  // RIRBUBASE

    // MSI trigger: 1-cycle pulse when INTFL transitions 0->1
    // We detect the rising edge of reg_0x00000060[0] (RIRBINTSTS.INTFL)
    reg intfl_prev;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            intfl_prev <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            intfl_prev <= reg_0x00000060[0];
        end
    end
    // MSI trigger gated by INTCTL: GIE (bit 31) and CIE (bit 30) must be enabled
    wire intctl_gie = reg_0x00000020[31];
    wire intctl_cie = reg_0x00000020[30];
    assign msi_trigger = reg_0x00000060[0] && !intfl_prev && intctl_gie && intctl_cie;
    assign rirbintsts  = reg_0x00000060;  // live RIRBINTSTS value
    assign crst_falling = !reg_0x00000008[0] && crst_prev;  // CRST falling edge

{{ end }}
```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_device_audio_response_fsm.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_audio_response_fsm" }}    // MMIO write detection for FSM-driven registers (0x48, 0x58).
    // These are excluded from the generic write case to avoid multi-driver
    // conflicts, so we detect and forward writes here.
    reg wr_0x48_pending, wr_0x58_pending;
    reg [31:0] wr_0x48_data, wr_0x58_data;
    reg [3:0]  wr_0x48_be,   wr_0x58_be;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            wr_0x48_pending <= 1'b0;
            wr_0x58_pending <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            wr_0x48_pending <= wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h00000048;
            wr_0x58_pending <= wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h00000058;
            wr_0x48_data    <= wr_data;
            wr_0x58_data    <= wr_data;
            wr_0x48_be      <= wr_be;
            wr_0x58_be      <= wr_be;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h00;
            rirb_fake_response <= 64'h0;
            corbwp_prev        <= 8'h00;
            rirb_pending_count <= 8'h00;
            rirb_wp_count      <= 8'h00;
            rirb_response_idx  <= 6'd0;
            corb_cte_prev      <= 1'b0;
            rirb_cte_prev      <= 1'b0;
            dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b0;
            dma_resp_lo_r      <= 32'h0;
            dma_resp_hi_r      <= 32'h0;
            dma_resp_wp_r      <= 8'h0;
            intfl_set_req      <= 1'b0;
            dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
            dma_round_count    <= 4'h0;
            // FSM-driven register resets (sole driver for these regs)
            reg_0x00000048     <= 32'h00000000;
            reg_0x00000058     <= 32'h00000000;
            reg_0x0000005C     <= 32'h00820000;
            reg_0x00000070     <= 32'h00000000;
            reg_0x00000074     <= 32'h00000000;
        end else begin
            // Default: no INTFL set request this cycle.
            // Response commit path below may set this to 1.
            intfl_set_req <= 1'b0;

            // CRST falling edge guard: if CRST is being asserted, suppress all
            // FSM activity this cycle. The CRST block (separate always block)
            // resets all state vars — we must not fight it with our own
            // assignments. Without this guard, both blocks drive the same regs
            // and the result is synthesis-tool-dependent.

            // Track CTE for reinitialization detection
            if (!crst_falling && !crst_rising) begin
                corb_cte_prev <= corb_cte;
                rirb_cte_prev <= rirb_cte;

                // corbwp_prev is NOT updated here - only when
                // corbwp_changed fires to avoid losing VERB deltas.
            end else if (crst_falling) begin
                corb_cte_prev <= 1'b0;
                rirb_cte_prev <= 1'b0;
                corbwp_prev   <= 8'h00;
            end

            // CRST rising edge: controller coming out of reset
            if (crst_rising) begin
                rirb_response_idx  <= 6'd0;
                rirb_pending_count <= 8'h00;
                rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h00;
                rirb_wp_count      <= 8'h00;
                corb_cte_prev      <= 1'b0;
                rirb_cte_prev      <= 1'b0;
                corbwp_prev        <= 8'h00;
                dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b0;
                dma_resp_lo_r      <= 32'h0;
                dma_resp_hi_r      <= 32'h0;
                dma_resp_wp_r      <= 8'h0;
                dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
                dma_round_count    <= 4'h0;
            end

            // CORB/RIRB reinitialization: driver disabled CTE → reset ROM index
            // and pending state so the next discovery cycle starts from index 0.
            // Guarded by !crst_falling — CRST block handles reset.
            //
            // This is critical: hdaudio.sys re-enumeration expects the same
            // discovery-phase responses (indices 0-19) as the first boot.
            // If we don't reset rirb_response_idx, we'll serve runtime-zone
            // responses to discovery VERBs, causing Code 10 on re-plug.
            if (rb_reinit && !crst_falling) begin
                rirb_response_idx  <= 6'd0;
                rirb_pending_count <= 8'h00;
                rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h00;
                rirb_wp_count      <= 8'h00;  // Reset WP — driver expects fresh buffer
                corbwp_prev        <= 8'h00;
                reg_0x00000048[23:16] <= 8'h00;  // reset CORBRP to 0
                reg_0x0000005C[9:8] <= 2'b0;  // clear RIRBSTS (RINTFL + OIS)
                // Clear DMA handshake state to prevent bridge from accepting
                // stale request data after reinit. Without this, if reinit
                // fires while FSM is in state 0x10/0x11, dma_req_valid_r
                // stays asserted and the bridge sends garbage TLPs.
                dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b0;
                dma_done_latched   <= 1'b0;
                dma_timed_out      <= 1'b0;
                dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
                dma_round_count    <= 4'h0;
                // NOTE: RIRBLBASE/RIRBUBASE preserved, driver may not reprogram
                // them on re-init if the buffer address hasn't changed.
            end

            // DMA done latch and timeout tracking
            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h11 && dma_done_latched) begin
                dma_done_latched <= 1'b0;
            end else if (dma_done) begin
                dma_done_latched <= 1'b1;
            end else if (rirb_response_fsm != 8'h11 && rirb_response_fsm != 8'h10) begin
                dma_done_latched <= 1'b0;
            end

            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h11) begin
                dma_wait_counter <= dma_wait_counter + 1'b1;
                if (dma_wait_counter >= 28'hFFFFFFF)
                    dma_timed_out <= 1'b1;
            end else begin
                dma_wait_counter <= 28'h0;
                dma_timed_out <= 1'b0;
            end

            // MMIO write forwarding for FSM-driven registers.

            // 0x48: CORBWP (bits 7:0 writable), CORBRPRST (bit 31 self-clear)
            // bits 23:16 (CORBRP) handled by FSM above, not host-writable.
            if (wr_0x48_pending && !rb_reinit && !crst_falling) begin
                if (wr_0x48_be[0]) reg_0x00000048[7:0]   <= (reg_0x00000048[7:0]   & ~8'hFF) | (wr_0x48_data[7:0]   & 8'hFF);
                if (wr_0x48_be[3]) reg_0x00000048[31]    <= wr_0x48_data[31];  // CORBRPRST
            end

            // 0x58: RIRBWPRST (bit 15 self-clear), RINTCNT (bits 31:16 writable)
            // bits 7:0 (RIRBWP) driven by FSM, not host-writable.
            if (wr_0x58_pending && !rb_reinit && !crst_falling) begin
                if (wr_0x58_be[1]) reg_0x00000058[15]    <= wr_0x58_data[15];  // RIRBWPRST
                if (wr_0x58_be[2]) reg_0x00000058[23:16] <= wr_0x58_data[23:16];
                if (wr_0x58_be[3]) reg_0x00000058[31:24] <= wr_0x58_data[31:24];
            end

            // RIRBCTL/RIRBSTS driver write - merged into FSM to avoid multi-driver
            if (rirbctl_rw1c && !rb_reinit) begin
                if (hda_wr_be[0]) begin
                    reg_0x0000005C[0] <= rirbctl_wr_rintctl_val;
                    reg_0x0000005C[1] <= rirbctl_wr_cte_val;
                    reg_0x0000005C[2] <= rirbctl_wr_oie_val;
                end
                if (hda_wr_be[1]) begin
                    reg_0x0000005C[10:8] <= reg_0x0000005C[10:8] & ~rirbsts_clear_mask;
                end
            end

            // RIRBWPRST: driver writes 1 to bit 15 of 0x58 to reset RIRBWP
            if (reg_0x00000058[15] && !crst_falling) begin
                rirb_wp_count <= 8'h00;
                reg_0x00000058[15] <= 1'b0;  // auto-clear RIRBWPRST
            end

            // CORBRPRST: driver writes 1 to bit 31 of 0x48 to reset CORBRP
            if (reg_0x00000048[31] && !crst_falling) begin
                reg_0x00000048[23:16] <= 8'h00;  // reset CORBRP to 0
                reg_0x00000048[31] <= 1'b0;  // auto-clear CORBRPRST
            end

            // Enqueue: add the actual number of entries the driver submitted.
            // Guard: if rb_reinit is active, ignore corbwp_changed in the same
            // cycle. Without this, a driver that changes CORBWP while disabling
            // CTE would leave a stale pending count after reinitialization.
            // Guarded by !crst_falling — CRST block handles reset.
            if (corbwp_changed && !rb_reinit && !crst_falling) begin
                // Saturating addition: prevent overflow when DMA is stuck.
                // If pending_count + delta would exceed 255, cap at 255.
                // Without this, overflow wraps to 0 and the FSM stops
                // producing responses, causing hdaudio.sys Code 10.
                if (rirb_pending_count + corbwp_delta < rirb_pending_count) begin
                    rirb_pending_count <= 8'hFF;
                end else begin
                    rirb_pending_count <= rirb_pending_count + corbwp_delta;
                end
                // Auto-advance CORB read pointer (controller consumed CORB entries)
                reg_0x00000048[23:16] <= reg_0x00000048[23:16] + corbwp_delta;
                // Snapshot CORBWP so next delta is calculated correctly
                corbwp_prev <= reg_0x00000048[7:0];
            end

            // All FSM transitions are guarded by !crst_falling to avoid fighting
            // with the CRST block which resets state vars in a separate always block.

            // Build response data when starting a new response
            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h00 && rirb_pending_count > 8'h00 && !crst_falling) begin
                // Look up the next response from the CA0132 ROM
                rirb_fake_response <= rirb_rom_response(rirb_response_idx);
                // Cycle: advance up to 63, then wrap to 32 (extended runtime zone).
                // Wrapping to 32 instead of 0 avoids re-sending discovery-phase
                // responses, which would confuse the driver during sustained operation.
                rirb_response_idx  <= (rirb_response_idx < 6'd63) ? rirb_response_idx + 6'h1 : 6'd32;
                rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h04; // 4-cycle delay before committing
            end

            // Response FSM countdown
            if (rirb_response_fsm > 8'h00 && rirb_response_fsm <= 8'h04 && !crst_falling) begin
                rirb_response_fsm <= rirb_response_fsm - 8'h01;

                // When FSM reaches 1, initiate DMA write handshake with bridge
                if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h01) begin
                    dma_req_valid_r <= 1'b1;
                    dma_resp_lo_r   <= rirb_fake_response[31:0];
                    // convert ROM custom format to HDA spec RESP_EX:
                    // ROM resp_hi[3:0] = type (1=solicited, 2=unsolicited)
                    // HDA spec RESP_EX: [3:0]=codec_addr, [4]=unsolicited
                    // all responses come from codec 0 (matches STATESTS bit 0)
                    dma_resp_hi_r   <= (rirb_fake_response[35:32] == 4'h2) ?
                                       32'h00000010 :  // codec 0, unsolicited
                                       32'h00000000;   // codec 0, solicited
                    dma_resp_wp_r   <= rirb_wp_count + 8'h01;
                    rirb_response_fsm <= 8'h10; // enter DMA accept wait (outside countdown range)
                end
            end

            // DMA handshake state machine (states 0x10/0x11, outside countdown range):
            //   0x10: wait for bridge to accept request (dma_req_ready)
            //   0x11: wait for bridge to complete write (dma_done)
            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h10 && dma_req_valid_r && dma_req_ready && !crst_falling) begin
                // Bridge accepted the request, clear our request
                dma_req_valid_r <= 1'b0;
                rirb_response_fsm <= 8'h11;
            end

            // Bridge recovery: if bridge timed out (returned to IDLE, dma_req_ready=1)
            // but we're still in state 0x11 waiting for dma_done, re-assert the request
            // so the bridge can accept it again with fresh data.
            // Only trigger recovery when neither success nor timeout is pending —
            // if dma_done_latched or dma_timed_out is set, other paths handle it
            // and retry would cause state corruption or permanent loop.
            // Limit: after 65536 recovery attempts, give up: the bridge is permanently
            // stuck (e.g. downstream AXI blocked). Abort this response so the FSM
            // can process remaining pending responses instead of freezing forever.
            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h11 && dma_req_ready && !dma_req_valid_r && !dma_done && !dma_done_latched && !dma_timed_out && !crst_falling) begin
                if (dma_recovery_count >= 16'hFFFF) begin
                    if (dma_round_count >= 4'hF) begin
                        // Bridge permanently stuck after 16 rounds.
                        // Last resort: commit via MMIO so driver makes progress.
                        rirb_wp_count <= rirb_wp_count + 8'h01;
                        reg_0x00000070[31:0] <= dma_resp_lo_r;
                        reg_0x00000074[31:0] <= dma_resp_hi_r;
                        if (dma_resp_hi_r[4])
                            reg_0x0000005C[9] <= 1'b1;
                        intfl_set_req <= 1'b1;
                        rirb_pending_count <= rirb_pending_count - 8'h01;
                        rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h00;
                        dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b0;
                        dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
                        dma_round_count    <= 4'h0;
                        dma_done_latched   <= 1'b0;
                        dma_timed_out      <= 1'b0;
                    end else begin
                        // Restart countdown with same response data in rirb_fake_response
                        rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h04;
                        dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b0;
                        dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
                        dma_round_count    <= dma_round_count + 4'h1;
                        dma_done_latched   <= 1'b0;
                        dma_timed_out      <= 1'b0;
                    end
                end else begin
                    // Bridge returned to IDLE: re-assert request for retry
                    dma_req_valid_r    <= 1'b1;
                    rirb_response_fsm  <= 8'h10;
                    dma_wait_counter   <= 28'h0;
                    dma_timed_out      <= 1'b0;
                    dma_recovery_count <= dma_recovery_count + 16'h1;
                end
            end

            if (rirb_response_fsm == 8'h11 && !crst_falling) begin
                // Waiting for DMA bridge to complete the write.
                // Use latched done signal to avoid missing the 1-cycle pulse.
                if (dma_done_latched) begin
                    // DMA write completed: now commit to MMIO registers

                    // Increment RIRBWP counter (8-bit, wraps at 256 per RIRBSIZE).
                    // Mask to RIRBSIZE: the size field at 0x5C[31:24] encodes
                    // supported buffer sizes. 0x40 = 256 entries (full 8-bit range).
                    // We mask to prevent WP from exceeding the programmed size.
                    rirb_wp_count <= rirb_wp_count + 8'h01;

                    // Write response data to MMIO response registers (for drivers
                    // that may fall back to reading these instead of DMA buffer).
                    reg_0x00000070[31:0] <= dma_resp_lo_r;
                    reg_0x00000074[31:0] <= dma_resp_hi_r;

                    // Set RIRBSTS.UIS for unsolicited responses
                    // RESP_EX bit 4 = unsolicited flag (set by format conversion above)
                    if (dma_resp_hi_r[4]) begin
                        reg_0x0000005C[9] <= 1'b1;
                    end

                    // Set RIRBINTSTS.INTFL: tells driver a response is available.
                    // Actual register write is handled by consolidated INTFL driver
                    // at end of FSM block; set flag so it can merge with clear requests.
                    intfl_set_req <= 1'b1;

                    // Decrement pending count (one response delivered)
                    rirb_pending_count <= rirb_pending_count - 8'h01;
                    dma_recovery_count <= 16'h0;
                    dma_round_count    <= 4'h0;

                    // Return to idle: ready for next CORB entry
                    rirb_response_fsm <= 8'h00;
                end else if (dma_timed_out) begin
                    // DMA bridge didn't respond within timeout: return to idle
                    // but PRESERVE pending_count. The response data remains
                    // latched in dma_resp_lo/hi/wp_r registers. On the next
                    // cycle, pending_count > 0 triggers a new response attempt
                    // with the same data, giving the bridge another chance.
                    // Only after bridge timeout+recovery cycle (16384+ cycles)
                    // does the request get re-submitted cleanly.
                    // Decrementing pending_count here would permanently lose
                    // the response, causing RIRBWP to stall and the driver
                    // to eventually timeout with Code 10.
                    // Clear stale latch to prevent false dma_done on next request.
                    dma_done_latched  <= 1'b0;
                    dma_timed_out     <= 1'b0;
                    rirb_response_fsm <= 8'h00;
                end
            end
        end
```

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_audio_response_rom" }}    // CA0132 codec response ROM — provides unique responses per VERB
    // so hdaudio.sys can complete codec topology discovery.
    // Format: {type_nid[31:0], response_data[31:0]}
    // type=1 in bits [3:0], NID in [27:4], tag in [31:28].
    //
    // Entries 0–19: initial codec discovery (node parameters, configs).
    // Entries 20–31: runtime responses (power state, pin sense, amp settings,
    //   extra nodes) to prevent catch-all saturation during extended operation.
    // Entries 32–63: extended runtime phase — cycling zone for repeated VERBs
    //   (power transitions, converter/stream queries, jack detect simulation,
    //   EAPD/BTL, repeated node parameters). After index 63, the counter wraps
    //   back to 32 (runtime zone) rather than 0 (discovery zone), preventing
    //   duplicate discovery responses during sustained operation.
    function [63:0] rirb_rom_response;
        input [5:0] idx;
        begin
            case (idx)
                // === DISCOVERY PHASE (indices 0–19) ===
                // 0: GET_PARAMETERS(Node 0 — AFG)
                // NumSubNodes=16 | StartNode=1 | FuncType=AFG(0x1)
                6'd0:  rirb_rom_response = {32'h00000001, 32'h01010001};
                // 1: GET_SUBSYSTEM_ID
                // SubsystemID = 0x11020010 (Creative SB Audigy FX)
                6'd1:  rirb_rom_response = {32'h00000001, 32'h11020010};
                // 2: GET_PARAMETERS(Node 1 — Audio Out, playback DAC)
                // OutAmp=0, InAmp=0, Cap=0x3 (Out+Stereo), Type=0x1
                6'd2:  rirb_rom_response = {32'h00000011, 32'h00030001};
```

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_ethernet" }}{{ if eq .DeviceClass "ethernet" }}
    // PHYAR/ERIAR done-flag auto-clear for r8169 driver.
    // Driver sets bit 31 and polls until it drops.
    // These registers are IsFSMDriven — sole driver is this always block.
    reg [2:0] phyar_cnt;
    reg       phyar_pending;
    reg [2:0] eriar_cnt;
    reg       eriar_pending;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            phyar_pending  <= 1'b0;
            phyar_cnt      <= 3'h0;
            eriar_pending  <= 1'b0;
            eriar_cnt      <= 3'h0;
            reg_0x000000DC <= 32'h80000000;  // PHYAR: bit31 = ready
            reg_0x000000E0 <= 32'h80000000;  // ERIAR: bit31 = done
        end else begin
            // MMIO write forwarding for PHYAR (0xDC)
            if (wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h000000DC) begin
                if (wr_be[0]) reg_0x000000DC[7:0]   <= wr_data[7:0];
                if (wr_be[1]) reg_0x000000DC[15:8]  <= wr_data[15:8];
                if (wr_be[2]) reg_0x000000DC[23:16] <= wr_data[23:16];
                if (wr_be[3]) reg_0x000000DC[31:24] <= wr_data[31:24];
                if (wr_data[31]) begin
                    phyar_pending <= 1'b1;
                    phyar_cnt     <= 3'h1;
                end
            end
            if (phyar_pending) begin
                phyar_cnt <= phyar_cnt + 1'b1;
                if (phyar_cnt >= 3'h4) begin
                    reg_0x000000DC[31] <= 1'b0;
                    phyar_pending      <= 1'b0;
                end
            end

            // MMIO write forwarding for ERIAR (0xE0)
            if (wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h000000E0) begin
                if (wr_be[0]) reg_0x000000E0[7:0]   <= wr_data[7:0];
                if (wr_be[1]) reg_0x000000E0[15:8]  <= wr_data[15:8];
                if (wr_be[2]) reg_0x000000E0[23:16] <= wr_data[23:16];
                if (wr_be[3]) reg_0x000000E0[31:24] <= wr_data[31:24];
                if (wr_data[31]) begin
                    eriar_pending <= 1'b1;
                    eriar_cnt     <= 3'h1;
                end
            end
            if (eriar_pending) begin
                eriar_cnt <= eriar_cnt + 1'b1;
                if (eriar_cnt >= 3'h4) begin
                    reg_0x000000E0[31] <= 1'b0;
                    eriar_pending      <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
    end
```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_device_msix.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_msix" }}{{ if .HasMSIX }}
    // ========================================================================
    // MSI-X Interrupt Controller - 4-state FSM
    //   IDLE -> PENDING -> ASSERT -> COOLDOWN
    // Triggered when a writable register is modified.
    // LFSR-based jitter prevents timing fingerprinting.
    // ========================================================================
    localparam [1:0] INT_IDLE     = 2'b00;
    localparam [1:0] INT_PENDING  = 2'b01;
    localparam [1:0] INT_ASSERT   = 2'b10;
    localparam [1:0] INT_COOLDOWN = 2'b11;

    reg [1:0]  int_state;
    reg [5:0]  int_counter;
    reg [5:0]  int_cooldown_target;
    reg        int_trigger;

    // 16-bit LFSR for interrupt timing jitter
    reg [15:0] int_lfsr;
    wire int_lfsr_fb = int_lfsr[15] ^ int_lfsr[14] ^ int_lfsr[12] ^ int_lfsr[3];

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst)
            int_lfsr <= {4'h0, 4'h{{ hex02 .DeviceIDs.RevisionID }}, 8'h{{ hex02 (index (rwMaskBytes (index .PRNGSeeds 0)) 0) }}};
        else
            int_lfsr <= {int_lfsr[14:0], int_lfsr_fb};
    end

    // Write activity detection - any write to a writable register triggers
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst)
            int_trigger <= 1'b0;
        else
            int_trigger <= wr_valid;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            int_state           <= INT_IDLE;
            int_counter         <= 6'h0;
            int_cooldown_target <= 6'h10;
        end else begin
            case (int_state)
                INT_IDLE: begin
                    if (int_trigger) begin
                        int_state   <= INT_PENDING;
                        int_counter <= 6'h0;
                    end
                end

                INT_PENDING: begin
                    int_counter <= int_counter + 1'b1;
                    // Random pending delay (2-6 cycles based on LFSR)
                    if (int_counter >= {4'h0, int_lfsr[1:0]} + 6'h2)
                        int_state <= INT_ASSERT;
                end

                INT_ASSERT: begin
                    // Assert for 1 cycle then cooldown
                    int_state <= INT_COOLDOWN;
                    int_counter <= 6'h0;
                    // Jittered cooldown (16-63 cycles)
                    int_cooldown_target <= {int_lfsr[5:4], 4'h0} + 6'h10;
                end

                INT_COOLDOWN: begin
                    int_counter <= int_counter + 1'b1;
                    if (int_counter >= int_cooldown_target)
                        int_state <= INT_IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
{{ end }}

{{ end }}
```

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_nvme" }}{{ if eq .DeviceClass "nvme" }}
    // ========================================================================
    // NVMe CC -> CSTS State Machine
    // stornvme.sys polls CSTS.RDY after writing CC.EN - this is the #1 cause
    // of Code 10. Static CSTS values do NOT work; real transition is required.
    // ========================================================================
    reg        cc_en_prev;
    reg [3:0]  csts_transition_cnt;
    reg        csts_rdy_pending;
    wire       cc_en_rising  = reg_0x00000014[0] && !cc_en_prev;
    wire       cc_en_falling = !reg_0x00000014[0] && cc_en_prev;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            cc_en_prev          <= 1'b0;
            csts_transition_cnt <= 4'h0;
            csts_rdy_pending    <= 1'b0;
            reg_0x0000001C      <= 32'h00000000;  // CSTS: RDY=0, CFS=0, SHST=0
        end else begin
            cc_en_prev <= reg_0x00000014[0]; // CC.EN

            // CC.EN rising edge -> start RDY transition (2-8 cycle delay)
            if (cc_en_rising) begin
                csts_rdy_pending    <= 1'b1;
                csts_transition_cnt <= 4'h0;
                reg_0x0000001C[0]   <= 1'b0;  // CSTS.RDY = 0 while enabling
            end
            // CC.EN falling edge -> controller disabled; SHST is only for CC.SHN shutdown
            else if (cc_en_falling) begin
                reg_0x0000001C[0]   <= 1'b0;  // CSTS.RDY = 0
                csts_rdy_pending    <= 1'b0;
                csts_transition_cnt <= 4'h0;
            end else if (csts_rdy_pending) begin
                // Pending RDY transition: count up then set RDY.
                csts_transition_cnt <= csts_transition_cnt + 1'b1;
                if (csts_transition_cnt >= 4'h4) begin
                    reg_0x0000001C[0] <= 1'b1;  // CSTS.RDY = 1
                    csts_rdy_pending  <= 1'b0;
                end
            end

            // SHST follows the live CC.SHN request and the responder's real
            // drain/flush/abort terminal acknowledgement.
            if (reg_0x00000014[15:14] == 2'b00)
                reg_0x0000001C[3:2] <= 2'b00;
            else if (nvme_shutdown_complete)
                reg_0x0000001C[3:2] <= 2'b10;
            else
                reg_0x0000001C[3:2] <= 2'b01;

            // A disable edge owns same-cycle priority over a fatal pulse.
            // Otherwise CFS is sticky until reset or the next CC.EN falling edge.
            if (cc_en_falling)
                reg_0x0000001C[1] <= 1'b0;
            else if (controller_fatal)
                reg_0x0000001C[1] <= 1'b1;
        end
    end
{{ end }}
{{ end }}
```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_device_xhci.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
{{ define "bar_impl_device_xhci" }}{{ if eq .DeviceClass "xhci" }}
    // xHCI HCRST auto-clear + R/S-HCH tracking.
    // USBCMD (0x20) and USBSTS (0x24) are IsFSMDriven — sole driver is this block.
    reg [3:0] hcrst_cnt;
    reg       hcrst_pending;

    // R/S -> HCH tracking: when driver sets R/S=1, HCH must clear.
    reg       rs_prev;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            hcrst_cnt      <= 4'h0;
            hcrst_pending  <= 1'b0;
            rs_prev        <= 1'b0;
            reg_0x00000020 <= 32'h00000001;  // USBCMD: R/S=1 (running)
            reg_0x00000024 <= 32'h00000000;  // USBSTS: HCH=0 (not halted)
        end else begin
            rs_prev <= reg_0x00000020[0]; // USBCMD.R/S

            // USBCMD byte-0 mask must include R/S (bit 0); dropping it breaks halt/run + HCRST sequencing.
            if (wr_valid && (wr_addr[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC) == 32'h00000020 && !hcrst_pending) begin
                if (wr_be[0]) reg_0x00000020[7:0]   <= (reg_0x00000020[7:0]   & ~8'h0F) | (wr_data[7:0]   & 8'h0F);
                if (wr_be[1]) reg_0x00000020[15:8]  <= (reg_0x00000020[15:8]  & ~8'h2F) | (wr_data[15:8]  & 8'h2F);
            end

            // HCRST handling
            if (reg_0x00000020[1] && !hcrst_pending) begin
                hcrst_pending <= 1'b1;
                hcrst_cnt     <= 4'h0;
            end
            if (hcrst_pending) begin
                hcrst_cnt <= hcrst_cnt + 1'b1;
                if (hcrst_cnt >= 4'h4) begin
                    reg_0x00000020[1] <= 1'b0;    // clear HCRST
                    reg_0x00000024    <= 32'h0001; // USBSTS = HCH (halted after reset)
                    hcrst_pending     <= 1'b0;
                end
            end

            // R/S rising edge -> clear HCH (controller running)
            if (reg_0x00000020[0] && !rs_prev && !hcrst_pending) begin
                reg_0x00000024[0] <= 1'b0;  // USBSTS.HCH = 0
            end

            // R/S falling edge -> set HCH (controller halted)
            if (!reg_0x00000020[0] && rs_prev && !hcrst_pending) begin
                reg_0x00000024[0] <= 1'b1;  // USBSTS.HCH = 1
            end
        end
    end
{{ end }}
{{ end }}
```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_impl_msi.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
//
// BAR implementation for MSI doorbell interrupt.
// Write to offset 0x00 triggers a single-cycle MSI interrupt pulse.
// Read from offset 0x00 returns the last written value.
//
// This provides a software-triggerable MSI interrupt mechanism: any
// driver that writes to BAR2 offset 0x00 will cause the FPGA to
// generate an MSI interrupt to the host.
//

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module pcileech_bar_impl_msi(
    input               rst,
    input               clk,

    input [31:0]        wr_addr,
    input [31:0]        wr_data,
    input [3:0]         wr_be,
    input               wr_valid,

    input [87:0]        rd_req_ctx,
    input [31:0]        rd_req_addr,
    input               rd_req_valid,

    output reg [87:0]   rd_rsp_ctx,
    output reg [31:0]   rd_rsp_data,
    output reg          rd_rsp_valid,

    output              intr_req
);

    reg [31:0]      doorbell;
    reg             intr_req_reg;
    reg [31:0]      doorbell_q;
    reg             rd_req_valid_q;

    // Read response: 2-cycle latency
    always @ ( posedge clk ) begin
        doorbell_q          <= doorbell;
        rd_req_valid_q      <= rd_req_valid;
        rd_rsp_ctx          <= rd_req_ctx;
        rd_rsp_data         <= doorbell_q;
        rd_rsp_valid        <= rd_req_valid_q;
    end

    // Write handling: capture doorbell value and pulse intr_req
    always @ ( posedge clk ) begin
        if ( rst ) begin
            doorbell    <= 32'h0;
            intr_req_reg <= 1'b0;
        end
        else if ( wr_valid ) begin
            if ( wr_be[0] ) doorbell[7:0]   <= wr_data[7:0];
            if ( wr_be[1] ) doorbell[15:8]  <= wr_data[15:8];
            if ( wr_be[2] ) doorbell[23:16] <= wr_data[23:16];
            if ( wr_be[3] ) doorbell[31:24] <= wr_data[31:24];
            intr_req_reg <= 1'b1;
        end
        else begin
            intr_req_reg <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    assign intr_req = intr_req_reg;

endmodule
```

```tmpl
    wire request_can_accept = !request_fifo_full || request_pop;
    wire request_push = tlps_in_valid && request_can_accept;

    function automatic [2:0] popcount4(input [3:0] value);
        begin
            popcount4 = {2'b00, value[0]} + {2'b00, value[1]} +
                        {2'b00, value[2]} + {2'b00, value[3]};
        end
    endfunction

    function automatic [1:0] first_enabled_offset(input [3:0] value);
        begin
            if (value[0])      first_enabled_offset = 2'd0;
            else if (value[1]) first_enabled_offset = 2'd1;
            else if (value[2]) first_enabled_offset = 2'd2;
            else if (value[3]) first_enabled_offset = 2'd3;
            else               first_enabled_offset = 2'd0;
        end
    endfunction

    function automatic [10:0] next_completion_dw(
        input [63:0] address_in,
        input [10:0] remaining_in
    );
        integer rcb_dw;
        integer mps_dw;
        integer selected_dw;
        begin
            rcb_dw = (READ_COMPLETION_BOUNDARY -
                      (address_in & (READ_COMPLETION_BOUNDARY - 1))) / 4;
            mps_dw = MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES / 4;
            selected_dw = remaining_in;
            if (selected_dw > rcb_dw)
                selected_dw = rcb_dw;
            if (selected_dw > mps_dw)
                selected_dw = mps_dw;
            next_completion_dw = selected_dw[10:0];
        end
    endfunction

    function automatic [12:0] completed_enabled_bytes(
        input [10:0] total_length,
        input [10:0] remaining_before,
        input [10:0] completion_length,
        input [3:0] first_enable,
        input [3:0] last_enable
    );
        reg [12:0] value;
        begin
            if (total_length == 11'd1) begin
                value = popcount4(first_enable);
            end else begin
                value = {completion_length, 2'b00};
                if (remaining_before == total_length)
                    value = value - (13'd4 - popcount4(first_enable));
                if (completion_length == remaining_before)
                    value = value - (13'd4 - popcount4(last_enable));
            end
            completed_enabled_bytes = value;
        end
    endfunction

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            req_wr_ptr <= 8'h00;
        end else if (request_push) begin
            req_addr_fifo[req_wr_ptr] <= norm_address;
            req_len_fifo[req_wr_ptr]  <= norm_length_dw;

        end
    end

    wire rd3_enable;

                                 ((remaining_dw == 11'd1) ? request_last_be : 4'hF);

                                ? {current_addr[31:2], packet_first_offset}

    assign rd_req_ctx = {

        packet_length_dw,

            state                 <= ST_IDLE;
            current_addr          <= 64'h0;
```

`internal/firmware/svgen/templates/bar_rsp_arbiter.sv.tmpl`:

```tmpl
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module pcileech_bar_rsp_arbiter (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst,
    input  wire [6:0]    in_valid,
    input  wire [87:0]   in_ctx [0:6],
    input  wire [31:0]   in_data [0:6],
    output wire [6:0]    in_ready,
    output wire          out_valid,
    output wire [87:0]   out_ctx,
    output wire [31:0]   out_data
);
    localparam integer FIFO_DEPTH = 32;
    reg [87:0] ctx_mem [0:6][0:FIFO_DEPTH-1];
    reg [31:0] data_mem [0:6][0:FIFO_DEPTH-1];
    reg [4:0] wr_ptr [0:6];
    reg [4:0] rd_ptr [0:6];
    reg [5:0] count [0:6];
    reg [2:0] rr_ptr;
    reg [2:0] selected;
    reg selected_valid;
    wire [6:0] push = in_valid & in_ready;
    genvar g;
    generate
        for (g = 0; g < 7; g = g + 1) begin : g_ready
            assign in_ready[g] = count[g] < 6'd32;
        end
    endgenerate
    integer scan;
    reg [3:0] index;
    always @* begin
        selected = 3'd0;
        selected_valid = 1'b0;
        for (scan = 0; scan < 7; scan = scan + 1) begin
            index = {1'b0, rr_ptr} + scan[3:0];
            if (index >= 4'd7)
                index = index - 4'd7;
            if (!selected_valid && count[index[2:0]] != 0) begin
                selected = index[2:0];
                selected_valid = 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end
    assign out_valid = selected_valid;
    assign out_ctx = selected_valid ? ctx_mem[selected][rd_ptr[selected]] : 88'h0;
    assign out_data = selected_valid ? data_mem[selected][rd_ptr[selected]] : 32'h0;
    integer k;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rr_ptr <= 3'd0;
            for (k = 0; k < 7; k = k + 1) begin
                wr_ptr[k] <= 5'd0;
                rd_ptr[k] <= 5'd0;
                count[k] <= 6'd0;
            end
        end else begin
            for (k = 0; k < 7; k = k + 1) begin
                if (push[k]) begin
                    ctx_mem[k][wr_ptr[k]] <= in_ctx[k];
                    data_mem[k][wr_ptr[k]] <= in_data[k];
                    wr_ptr[k] <= wr_ptr[k] + 5'd1;
                end
                if (selected_valid && selected == k[2:0])
                    rd_ptr[k] <= rd_ptr[k] + 5'd1;
                case ({push[k], selected_valid && selected == k[2:0]})
                    2'b10: count[k] <= count[k] + 6'd1;
                    2'b01: count[k] <= count[k] - 6'd1;
                    default: count[k] <= count[k];
                endcase
            end
            if (selected_valid)
                rr_ptr <= selected == 3'd6 ? 3'd0 : selected + 3'd1;
        end
    end
endmodule

`default_nettype wire
```
